newsitem.title: FRANCE: HORSE RACING-VEREVA GIVES AGA KHAN ANOTHER CLASSIC TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-VEREVA GIVES AGA KHAN ANOTHER CLASSIC TRIUMPH.

text.p: The progressive filly
Vereva gave her owner the Aga Khan a second French classic win
of the season in the French Oaks at Chantilly on Sunday.
The half sister to the high class Valanour, ridden by Gerald
Mosse, took up the running in the final 200 metres and held on
readily from the fast-finishing Mousse Glacee, the mount of
Thierry Thulliez.
Ryafan, Palme d'Or, Dances With Dreams and Brilliance had
formed the leading quartet turning into the straight before
Vereva made her decisive move.
Vereva quickened past the Ryafan and although Mousse Glacee,
who did not enjoy the clearest of runs, finished strongly the
damage had been done.
Vereva kept on well to win by a length and a half from
Mousse Glacee, with the favourite Brilliance a further two
lengths back in third in the field of 12.
Although there was a stewards enquiry prompted by outsider
La Nana leaning onto Mousse Glacee, who in turn did Brilliance
no favours, the finishing order was maintained.
However, the best filly on the day won as Vereva made it
three successes in as many starts on a softish track.
Winning trainer, Alain de Royer-Dupre, said: "We would
probably have started her off earlier but for a bout of
coughing.
"She is still an inexperienced filly but one with a lot of
quality and one for who plans remain fluid at this stage. We
shall go one step at the time."
Trainer Jean Lesbordes said Mousse Glacee, who was coming off
a poor run in the French 1,000 Guineas, will now head for the
Irish Oaks.
The Aga Khan-de Royer-Dupre team had previously teamed up to
win this race in 1993 with Shemaka. Earlier this season, the
pair took the French 2,000 Guineas with Daylami.
